messages:
ashley: Heads up — RFC follow-up: trying to simplify the tenant geo fallback matrix. Current state has too many per-tenant overrides and special cases. Proposal: collapse into three tiers: strict-residency, soft-residency, global-fallback. Thoughts? cc @surya @marta
surya: Agree we should simplify. Need to define exact semantics for soft-residency — e.g., reads allowed cross-region under latency-based conditions, writes always resident. Also what happens to KV cache ownership when we route reads elsewhere?
marta: :thumbsup: My draft semantics: soft-residency = prefer resident region for reads; if resident p95 > 500ms then serve from nearest region with a warning header + async backfill. Writes always to resident region; fallback behavior can be read-only or reject (configurable).
kevin: Concern: for EU regulated customers async backfill is unacceptable. We must keep strict-residency that never leaves region and defaults to reject-on-write or sync-failure.
ashley: Agreed — strict-residency remains an explicit tier. Goal is to reduce the combinatorial explosion of custom overrides. Global-fallback = best-effort serve anywhere with logging and explicit customer opt-in for cross-region writes.
ops-oncall: Operational Q: how do we signal resident "unreachable" today? We use lease + healthchecks but see flapping during upgrades and rolling restarts. That makes fallback noisy.
surya: We should use a quarantine heuristic: require 2 consecutive 10s failures OR 30s sustained p95 above threshold before marking unreachable. That reduces noisy flips during deploys.
infra-bot: deploy-status: canary policy change deployed to staging at 2026-03-20T12:04Z
ashley: Also need a compact config schema. Draft per-tenant YAML below for discussion:
```
fallback_policy: soft-residency
resident_region: eu-west-1
quarantine:
  failure_count: 2
  window_seconds: 10
read_fallback:
  allow_cross_region_reads: true
  latency_threshold_ms: 500
write_fallback:
  mode: reject_with_409
  async_forward: false
allow_stale_reads: false
```
marta: Looks reasonable. Add telemetry: header "X-Redwood-Residency-Active" on responses and metric `tenant.residency.fallback.count` with tags {tenant_id, policy, from_region, to_region}.
kevin: Edge-case: if we start serving reads cross-region, resident KV cache misses will spike when clients reconcile. We need pre-warm/backfill or a soft-cache-ownership model to avoid thundering. Suggest a soft TTL and backfill queue for hot keys.
surya: Add a flag `allow_stale_reads` (true/false) with `stale_ttl_seconds` for soft-residency. For strict-residency default is false. That gives ops a lever to trade freshness vs availability.
ashley: Rollout plan proposal: 1) add config schema + validation + tests, 2) deploy policy engine change to staging, 3) run canary on 5-10 low-traffic tenants, 4) run compliance regression tests with strict-residency tenants, 5) ramp to 50% then 100%.
ops-oncall: Please add runbook: manual cutover steps, rollback flag name, oncall contact list, and automated alert when fallback rate > 1% for >5m. Also include incident playbook for quarantine-oscillation.
marta: :white_check_mark: I'll draft the PR with schema, unit tests, and basic metrics wiring today.
nashley: Thanks — @infra-bot please kick off canary once PR merged.
infra-bot: ci-status: PR merged, canary rollout scheduled for 2026-03-20T14:00Z
kevin: One last note — ensure API responses for cross-region reads include a subtle emittable header we can surface in logs so downstream customers can opt to log sync/backfill events.
surya: Good call. Also we should add an internal dashboard card for tenant fallback churn so SRE can spot misconfigurations quickly.
ashley: Ok that's actionable. We'll iterate on the quarantine thresholds and the stale-read flag during canary. Thanks all.
